summary: FY2024 budget figures are the DRAFT (Oct 2023), not the adopted budget
detail: The adopted FY2024 budget (FY2024_budget, 'Budget Report by Fund - All', Dec 2023) is a scan OCR could not read reliably (dotted rules ruin the numbers). Until it is keyed from the page images, the FY2024 draft (layout B, ties to every printed subtotal) stands in for it. Draft and adopted differ: e.g. the adopted CIP revenue total is 724,600 against 720,400 in the draft. Facts built from the draft carry this exception; replace when the adopted document is extracted.

summary: Fund codes change between FY2024 and FY2025 documents
detail: FY2019-FY2024 documents number the funds 01 Corporate, 02 Recreation, 03 Museum, 09 Special Recreation, 10 Installment Contracts, 12 Bond & Interest, 21 CIP (FY2019-20 also 25 Riverfront); FY2025-FY2027 number them 01 General, 02 Recreation, 05 Special Recreation, 08 Museum, 10 Alternate Bond & Interest, 12 Bond & Interest, 21 Capital Projects. Museum and Special Recreation swap their codes; fund 10 changes its name. Joins across years go through entities/belvidere_park_district/funds.csv, not the code.

summary: Account numbers change from FF-DDDD-OOO to FF-DDD-OOOO in the FY2025 budget
detail: FY2019-FY2024: fund-department(4 digits)-object(3 digits), e.g. 01-0100-310 Corporate Real Estate Taxes. FY2025-FY2027: fund-department(3 digits)-object(4 digits), e.g. 01-010-3010. The department and object codes are renumbered, so the account map carries both formats and joins on a stable account concept, not on the number.

summary: Six FY2019 CIP accounts print without an object code
detail: The FY2019 budget prints Aberdeen Path overlay, Financial Software Purchase, Land Acquisition upgrades, Rivers Edge Soffit Repairs, HVAC control replacement and RTU Replacement as `21-0910-` with no object code. The extract keys them 21-0910-NONE-<label> (flag no_object_code).

summary: Rivers Edge Birthdays block has no printed total but is added by the city's Recreation grand total
detail: The 700 of Rivers Edge Birthdays lines are not in any block total (the Doty Park total is 101,085, its own lines), yet Grand Total Recreation Expenses (1,888,095) and the SUMMARY include them. The extract closes the block as an unprinted block (kind block_unprinted).

summary: FY2020 'Total Other Funds Income / Expenses' repeat the FY2019 figures
detail: The FY2020 page prints 3,949,967.00 and 3,390,830.89, the same numbers as the FY2019 document; the FY2020 blocks sum to 2,884,170 and 4,344,053, which the SUMMARY page prints. The two printed totals are not used.

summary: FY2020 Total Meehan Expenses (2,000) is 1,000 above its only line
detail: The Recreation grand total and SUMMARY add the printed 2,000, so the city's totals include a 1,000 that no line carries.

summary: The FY2022 budget PDF has only the expenditure report
detail: Six pages, 'Expenditure Budget Version Report'; there is no revenue report, so FY2022 has expenses only (the FY2022 appropriation ordinance and the audit may carry revenue).

summary: Amended revenue report: Cip Subtotal in the Original column is stale by 1,004
detail: It prints 880,796.00 (the FY2023 draft's figure); its lines and the Report Total Revenue (6,921,464.00) carry the adopted 881,800.00. Both copies of the report (text layer and scan) show it.

summary: Two copies of the FY2023 amended report hold identical figures
detail: FY2023_budget_amended (text layer, page headed DRAFT) and FY2023_budget_amended_oct (scan posted October 2023) agree on all 313 accounts; the owner confirmed both are final. The scan also has the amended appropriation ordinance 23-10-24A. Use one copy; the Original Budget column equals the FY2023 adopted budget on every shared account.

summary: Seven audit budget-and-actual variances carry the wrong sign for a financing line with a zero budget
detail: FY2023 General (Proceeds from sale of capital assets), FY2024 General (Subscription liability proceeds), FY2025 Capital Projects (Proceeds from sale of capital assets) print the variance with the opposite sign to actual minus budget; the net change (and the FY2025 Total other financing) variances carry the error through. Actual and budget columns are right; recorded as allow_diff in data/belvidere_park_district/overrides/FY20XX_audit.csv.

summary: FY2019 audit budget revenue differs from the budget document: General +50, Special Recreation +500 (document higher)
detail: Expenses match in every fund. The FY2019 budget document's General and Special Recreation income totals tie to their own lines and SUMMARY, so the audit's original budget differs from the adopted document by these amounts; not explained.

summary: FY2023 audit General Fund original budget: revenue 23,500 and expenditures 499.90 below the budget document
detail: The document and both amended reports (Original column) agree with each other (revenue 1,788,290, expenditures 1,787,870.90); the audit prints 1,764,790 and 1,787,371. Not explained (the revenue gap equals Memorials 22,500 plus Citations 1,000, which may be coincidence).

summary: FY2023 audit Special Recreation original budget revenue (569,038) is the draft's figure, the adopted document says 566,038
detail: 569,038 is the Special Recreation Subtotal in the FY2023 draft budget; the adopted budget and the amended report's Original column print 566,038.

summary: FY2024 audit vs budget compares against the DRAFT: Bond & Interest expense +880, Capital Projects expense -879.65
detail: The other five funds' revenue and expenses match to the dollar; these two differences are between the draft and the adopted budget the audit used (see EX-fy2024-budget-placeholder).

summary: FY2025 audit Recreation budget (1,962,057) is 36,000 above the budget document's current budget (1,926,057)
detail: Revenue and expenditures both; the audit's Original & Final budget probably includes a 2025 amendment that the December 2024 document predates. Not confirmed.

summary: FY2025 audit Capital Projects budget: 1,500 below the document on both revenue and expenditures; GO bond proceeds (810,200) are other financing in the audit
detail: The audit books bond proceeds as other financing, the budget document as revenue (explains 810,200 of the 811,700 revenue gap); the remaining 1,500 matches the expenditure gap.

summary: FY2020 audit Recreation budget expenditures are 2,500 below the budget document
detail: Revenue and the other six funds match to the dollar; not explained.

summary: FY2021 audit budgets differ from the budget document in four funds
detail: General: expenditures 76,733 and revenue 13,000 below the document's; Recreation: expenditures 73,692 and revenue 13,000 above; Special Recreation revenue 5,000 above; Capital Projects expenditures 66,848.71 below. The two large General/Recreation gaps run in opposite directions (net 3,041), which points to lines the audit books in the other fund or a mid-year amendment; not explained. Museum, Bond & Interest and Alternate Bond & Interest match.

summary: FY2022 audit Alternate Bond & Interest expenditures are 16,945 above the budget document's; revenue not comparable
detail: The FY2022 budget PDF has only the expenditure report (EX-fy2022-no-revenue-report). The other six funds' expenditures match to the dollar.

summary: FY2024 audit restates beginning compensated absences from 34,806 to 68,034 (GASB 101)
detail: The FY2024 audit adopts GASB Statement No. 101 (Compensated Absences) and restates the beginning balance and beginning net position; the FY2023 audit's ending balance (34,806) is therefore not the FY2024 beginning balance (68,034). Recorded as an explained difference in audit_debt_crosschecks.csv.

summary: FY2020 debt note 'retired' for the 2012A bonds (5,235,000) includes 4,885,000 advance-refunded through the escrow agent
detail: The statement of changes' debt service principal (2,450,000) excludes the refunded amount (payment to refunded bond escrow agent is an other financing use): 7,335,000 retired in the note - 4,885,000 = 2,450,000.

summary: FY2020 debt annual requirements: the 2031-2032 row restored (975,000 principal, 39,500 interest)
detail: OCR garbled the row; restored from the printed Total row and the same series in later audits (overrides/FY2020_audit_debt.csv).

summary: Audit expenditure classes and budget object categories are drawn differently
detail: The audits print Personnel, Contractual services, Material & supplies and Capital outlay; the budget classifies by object, and its object codes changed in FY2025 (4xxx personnel, 5xxx services, 6xxx supplies and maintenance). The groups are compared (personnel, contractual, supplies + capital, debt service) in audit_categories_vs_budget.csv: of 107 fund-year-groups 32 agree to the dollar, 60 are within 1% and 76 within 5%; the General Fund FY2019 and FY2020 groups differ by at most 0.2%. After the audits' classes for uniforms, course work material and travel / mileage reimbursement (Material & supplies) the budget's were moved to match (account_map.csv). The differences in a fund-year net to the fund-year's total difference, so they are reclassifications, not missing money.

summary: FY2023 appropriation and levy ordinances: three fund totals are below their own lines
detail: Corporate Fund total 1,427,019.90 is 500 below its purposes (1,427,519.90); Recreation Fund total 1,776,793.23 is 3,000 below (1,779,793.23); Bond and Interest total 2,596,952 is 90 below (2,597,042); Special Recreation is 9 cents off in the appropriation. The appropriation's SUMMARY OF FUNDS (c) uses the lines, the fund totals use the printed totals. The audit's original budget follows the printed totals. The appropriation's Section 3(e) estimate of taxes ($4,218,285.00, read on the page image) is 100 above the levy ordinance's aggregate ($4,218,185.00). The extracts keep the printed figures; the lines are kept beside them.

summary: FY2023 appropriation SUMMARY (b) revenue is the budget's total, 23,500 above the fund tables
detail: The summary's cash expected from all sources (6,924,464) is the budget document's total revenue; the fund revenue tables add to 6,900,964 (the Corporate table omits Memorials 22,500 and Citations 1,000). The audit's original budget revenue follows the fund tables.

summary: FY2019 ordinance: Riverfront Fund estimated year-end balance prints 0.00
detail: Beginning balance 2,336 + revenue 100 - appropriation 52,436 is -50,000; a transfer into the fund is implied but not printed.

summary: FY2021 ordinance: Bond and Interest revenue total is 800 below its lines
detail: Lines add to 2,359,131, the printed total is 2,358,331 (read on the page image).

summary: FY2022 ordinance Bond and Interest appropriation is 16,945 above the budget's
detail: The ordinance's Bond and Interest Fund appropriation (2,501,740) is above the budget's Bond & Interest + Installment + CIP expense lines; SUMMARY (c) uses the budget's total.

summary: FY2022 levy ordinance: its 'Appropriated' column is the FY2021 appropriation
detail: The Corporate (1,312,585) and Recreation (1,871,046) appropriated totals equal the FY2021 appropriation ordinance; the 'levied' amounts (Recreation 874,912 etc.) equal the FY2022 appropriation's tax revenue. The Museum total (205,035) is 13,650 below its lines (leaves out Repairs) and the IMRF total line prints no figure. The levy amounts are used; the appropriated lines are not a FY2022 budget.

summary: FY2024 levy: the aggregate leaves out the 50,000 Prior Year Adjustment; Debt Service total is 400 above its lines
detail: The aggregate levy (4,329,577.45) equals the fund levies without the Prior Year Adjustment (50,000, a county clerk shortfall for Special Recreation from taxes levied in 2021, which the Special Recreation levy of 327,734 already includes). The FY2023 aggregate includes the adjustment. The Debt Service Total Expenditures (2,446,800) is 400 above its purposes (2,446,400).

summary: FY2025 levy: Social Security section prints 169,550, the SUMMARY and aggregate use 173,840
detail: The section's levy (verified on the page image) is 4,290 below the SUMMARY line; the aggregate levy 4,533,060 follows the SUMMARY.

summary: District population is the district's FY2025 figure scaled by the city's Census series
detail: No published population series follows the park district's boundary (the Belvidere Township Park District is larger than the city and not a Census geography). The district's FY2025 AFR reports 32,342; earlier and later years are that figure times the city's July 1 estimate of the year over the city's 2025 estimate (25,462), a constant ratio of 1.2702. Per-resident park figures therefore follow the city's growth; they do not measure the district's own.
